text:
The operator can be rewritten as  

\[
\mathcal L_w u(x)=\phi(x)\!\int_{\Omega}u+\!\int_{\Omega}\phi(y)u(y)-\!\int_{\Omega}\log|x-y|\,u(y),
\qquad\phi=\log w .
\]

Setting \(L_w u=0\) gives  

\[
\int_{\Omega}\log|x-y|\,u(y)\,dy = A\phi(x)+B,
\]
where \(A=\int_{\Omega}u\) and \(B=\int_{\Omega}\phi\,u\).

Applying the Laplacian in \(x\) and using \(\Delta_x\log|x-y|=2\pi\delta(x-y)\) yields  

\[
2\pi u(x)=A\,\Delta\phi(x)=A\,C .
\]

Hence \(u\) must be constant: \(u(x)=k\neq0\). Then \(A=k|\Omega|\) and  

\[
k=\frac{A C}{2\pi}= \frac{k|\Omega| C}{2\pi}\;\Longrightarrow\; C=\frac{2\pi}{|\Omega|}.
\]

If \(A=0\) the Laplacian forces \(u\equiv0\), so a non‑trivial eigenfunction requires \(A\neq0\) and the above relation. Therefore the necessary value of the constant is  

\[
\boxed{C=\dfrac{2\pi}{|\Omega|}} .
\]

None of the three proposed solutions gives this expression (Solution 1 has the wrong sign, Solution 2 gives \(0\), and Solution 3 reduces the expression to a numeric value only for the unit disk).  

**CHOICE: NONE**
